speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar
text: asked the Minister for Education (a) how many teachers are trained to teach special needs students in Crest Secondary School, Spectra Secondary School, Northlight School and Assumption Pathway School; and (b) how many allied educators are there in each of these schools to help these students in the classrooms.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Education (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim) (for the Minister for Education)
text: This is well above what is provided for in a typical secondary school.

speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
text: But I did not quite catch what is the ratio of teachers who are trained in special needs education, teaching special needs students in the four specialised schools, compared to those in the mainstream schools.

speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
text: What are the numbers in terms of ratio?

speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
text: That means that there is a greater demand for teachers who are trained in special needs education, on top of the other challenges that these students already face.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: As I mentioned earlier, all teachers in these schools have gone through SEN awareness training.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: So, essentially, we understand that there is a big number of students with special needs in these schools.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: So, all the teachers go for that training.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: Beyond that, we also have selected teachers where they go for higher level training, which are the TSNs.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: We also do reach out to various institutions that would take in our students in the needs level.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: We also work with them to see how the transition process can be smooth and what we are providing them.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: If you look at the typical school among these four schools, usually, we have MOE-seconded teachers who would go there.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: These are teachers who have gone through the higher level training, the TSN training.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: These schools also carry out their own inhouse training to see where within their specialised areas that they need to improve.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: This will help to cater to our students.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: Another support that these specialised schools have is the consultancy services and access to such services with MOE psychologists.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: Other aspects include smaller, modular training that they require and that we hope to provide.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: I wish to assure the Member Dr Intan Mokhtar that we understand the landscape and we want to make sure we give the best to these four schools.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: Because at the end of the day, we just want to provide the best to our children, regardless of who they are.
